validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE all check out clean and are unusually well documented for this cohort. This is the Midcontinent Supply Header Interstate Pipeline Project (MIDSHIP), FERC Docket CP17-458, an interstate natural gas transmission pipeline correctly classified (Fuel=Gas, transmission trunk, not gathering). Application filed with FERC in 2017 (docket year prefix + offshore-technology.com), certificated Aug 13, 2018 (164 FERC P 61,103), construction authorized in stages Dec 2018-Feb 2019 and physically commenced 'in early 2019' per FERC's own order (174 FERC P 61,220, issued 2021-03-18, https://www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2021-03/C-5-CP17-458-000.pdf), completed installation March 2020, placed in service April 2020 -- corroborated by Pipeline & Gas Journal (2020-04-23, https://pgjonline.com/news/2020/04-april/cheniere-energy-midship-pipeline-approved-for-service), Power Progress (https://www.powerprogress.com/8003626.article), the EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (Historical Projects tab, row 'Cheniere MIDSHIP Pipeline Project': Completed Date 2020-04-16, Docket CP17-458, Authority FERC), and current 2026 trade press confirming continuous operation since (Natural Gas Intelligence, 2026-06-05, 'HEP Takes Full Midship Control...', https://www.naturalgasintel.com/news/hep-takes-full-midship-control-adds-midcontinent-natural-gas-gathering-lines/ -- 'throughput and utilization have set records since it began operating the pipeline'). Roster check: P0284 is the only Midship-related row in the 45-row batch; no relabel/duplicate found. One immaterial spec note: independent sources put total system length at ~234.1 mi (FERC's Federal Register EIS notice: 199.7 mi 36-in mainline + 20.5 mi 30-in Chisholm Lateral + 13.8 mi 16-in Velma Lateral + 0.1 mi 24-in tie-in = 234.1 mi; Pipeline & Gas Journal independently says 'nearly 234 miles') against the sheet's 233.00 mi -- a <0.5% rounding-level difference, not a material discrepancy (see Length [ref] fill for the REFS_ADDED treatment). Also for the record, not raised as a live concern since it never affected operating status: FERC issued a stop-work order for environmental non-compliance in July 2019 (resolved within a month) and a 2021 order directing restoration remediation on some landowner tracts -- historical construction-era friction, not a current defect.

validity.recommendation: update Owner1/Owner1% and Operator from the shell certificate-holder name to the current ultimate owner/operator, Howard Energy Partners (100%) -- Cheniere/EIG sold out in 2025-2026
validity.researcher_notes: Ownership is stale and was arguably mis-modeled even before the current stale-ness: the sheet's Owner1 = 'Midship Pipeline Co LLC' 100%, i.e. the pipeline's own certificate-holder LLC listed as its own 'owner' rather than naming the ultimate parent (the roster's own convention elsewhere names the parent, e.g. 'Black Bear Transmission LLC' for AlaTenn/Ozark). From 2017 to Feb 2025, Midship was 'indirectly and jointly owned by Cheniere and EIG' (EIG Global Energy Partners made a $500M equity investment in June 2017; Cheniere press release 2019-03-01, https://lngir.cheniere.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/180/cheniere-and-eig-complete-financing-and-issue-full-notice, does not disclose the exact split). On 2025-02-13, Howard Energy Partners (HEP, San Antonio) closed on an acquisition of equity interests in Midship from a subsidiary of Cheniere Energy and assumed operatorship -- Oil & Gas Journal, https://www.ogj.com/general-interest/companies/article/55268030/howard-energy-partners-acquires-operating-interest-in-midship-natural-gas-pipeline ('HEP assumed operatorship of the Midship Pipeline'). On 2026-05-29, HEP 'lifted its interest in Midship to 100%,' i.e. bought out whatever stake remained (Cheniere's residual and/or EIG's) -- Natural Gas Intelligence, 2026-06-05, https://www.naturalgasintel.com/news/hep-takes-full-midship-control-adds-midcontinent-natural-gas-gathering-lines/ ('Howard Energy Partners (HEP) has bought out the remaining stake in the Midship Pipeline, taking full ownership... The San Antonio-based midstream operator said it lifted its interest in Midship to 100% on May 29, more than a year after it first bought an operating stake from a subsidiary of Cheniere Energy and took over running the line'), confirmed independently by HEP's own release (https://www.howardenergypartners.com/howard-energy-partners-expands-midcontinent-platform-with-strategic-acquisitions/). Two independent trade-press origins (OGJ + NGI) plus the operator's own statement agree on both the Feb-2025 transfer and the May-2026 100% consolidation -- high tier. The FERC-certificated entity name itself likely remains 'Midship Pipeline Company, LLC' (matches the caption on FERC's own 2021 order and EIA's docket listing) -- that is why the Operator [ref] fill below is left as REFS_ADDED for the existing entity-name value rather than force-changed, but the contested block here flags that the entity's controlling owner/operator is now HEP, not itself, and recommends the researcher decide whether Operator should read the legal entity name or the controlling operator per current schema convention.
